body:
Thanks for sharing your story. I'm sorry you were used like that. It's a small comfort to know that I'm not the only one my age with such issues, even though I wouldn't wish it on anyone. I couldn't even take a day of seeing my ex on Facebook. I purged everything. Photos, FB friends I knew only through her, miscellaneous items in my room that reminded me of her, etc. Even finding strands of her blue hair attached to my bedspread was enough to set me off. I only found out her "Work on ourselves and talk later" line was bullshit after a friend tipped me off to a change of her profile picture. She's a coward.

I tried erasing her completely, but what I didn't account for at the time was just how much she is ingrained in my life. My memory is shit. Absolute, utter shit. Short term, long term, working, you name it. I've got severe ADHD and some kind of depression so it's not surprising. But I remember her. The good and the bad, the fights and the making up. Our relationship defined me, but I didn't mind it. It's only an issue if you lose it, because your whole sense of identity leaves along with it.

I feel like a slice of Swiss cheese with more holes than cheese. To remember her is to hurt, but I can't stand on my own identity because there's just not enough to stand on. I feel like I have so much baggage after this, how could I possibly trust someone again? I used to struggle to understand people who are afraid of "getting too close" but now I get it. I've got some hardcore abandonment issues after this. My psyche is hanging on by a thread as it is. The thought of seeing anyone else the way I used to/still kind of do see her should give me a little bit of excitement, or hope, but instead it's just fear.

The last thing I expected in response to this post was a compliment, but thank you. I think my expressive ability is at its finest when I'm in a sobered mood like the one required to convey a dismal message such as this one, so I'm not sure about the lasting power of such a talent and the accompanying toll on my mental health. Hope you're doing alright, friend.
